newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates close up, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates close up, seen rising.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed up on Saturday and are likely to open higher after Sunday's weekend holiday owing to a shortage of good-quality supplies from the old 1996/97 (July-June) crop, dealers said.
Spinners' preference for the old crop pushed the rates up, dealer Nasim Usman at the Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said.

The 1997/98 crop from southern Pakistan has reached the market but spinners are taking interest in the old crop, he said. In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was quoted for 2,375/2,385 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), the K-68 for 2,575/2,590 and the MNH-93 for 2,580/2,590.

KCA said exporters had shipped 125,515 bales (375 lbs each) of cotton by June 28 compared to 1.82 million in the same time a year ago. Exporters had registered contracts for the export of 164,756 bales by July 8 compared to 2.32 million in the same time a year ago.
